clue.text: Short visit to one company producing cotton cloth

indicators.note: something cut short loses its end, so the word for visit drops its final letter

blocks.note: to call on someone is to visit them
the Roman numeral for one
standard abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A brief call on a single firm that makes cotton fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Calico is a plain-woven fabric made from unbleached cotton, so it is a kind of cotton cloth.

clue.text: Quickly cut up thick slice of meat

blocks.note: to chop is to cut into pieces
a chop is a thick cut of pork or lamb

explanation.surface: Briskly carving a thick piece of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Chop-chop is an informal exhortation meaning hurry up, so it functions as an adverb for quickly.

clue.text: Fruit — stack Irish county's produced

blocks.note: a lime is a citrus fruit
a rick is a stack of hay

explanation.surface: An Irish county's harvest: fruit and haystacks.
explanation.definitionFit: Limerick is a county in the west of Ireland, in the province of Munster.

clue.text: Settlement, mostly in Costa Rican currency

indicators.note: mostly means not entirely, so the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: a colony is a settlement in a new territory

explanation.surface: A settlement paying largely in Costa Rica's money.
explanation.definitionFit: The colón is the monetary unit of Costa Rica, named after Christopher Columbus.

clue.text: Move through Dover, say, showing entry permit?

blocks.note: to pass is to go through
Dover is a well-known English ferry port; 'say' marks it as an example

explanation.surface: Travelling through Dover means showing your travel document at the border.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is loose: the document is not strictly a permit to enter, but it gets you in.
explanation.definitionFit: A passport is the official document a traveller presents to be allowed into a country.

clue.text: The maid and I, we got excited about British hymn

indicators.note: people who get excited are stirred up, so the letters are stirred into a new order
about means around, so the jumbled letters wrap round the abbreviation that follows

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
B is the abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: A servant and her employer, thrilled by a British church song.
explanation.walkthrough: The joining 'and' is left out of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Abide with Me is a Victorian Christian hymn by Henry Lyte, sung at funerals and the FA Cup final.

clue.text: Frustrate crowd with late news

blocks.note: to stop someone is to thwart them
a press is a dense throng of people

explanation.surface: Thwarting the throng that comes bearing late news.
explanation.definitionFit: Stop press is the space in a newspaper for news added at the last moment before printing.

clue.text: Fruit — round variety

blocks.note: the letter O is round
a range is an assortment or variety

explanation.surface: A spherical type of fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: An orange is a round citrus fruit, an obvious example of fruit.

clue.text: Oppressive ruler of party ran Tanzania

indicators.note: of here means made from part of, so the letters come from inside the words that follow

blocks.note: spans the end of party, all of ran and the start of Tanzania

explanation.surface: A despot whose party governed Tanzania.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyrant is a cruel ruler with absolute power who oppresses the people.

clue.text: Outlandish loo, rum in gold leaf

indicators.note: outlandish means bizarre and out of the ordinary, so the letters are pushed into a strange new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bizarre lavatory with rum in it, decorated in gilt.
explanation.definitionFit: Ormolu is gilded bronze or brass, gold applied as a thin leaf or powder for decorating furniture.

clue.text: Monster road in US under construction

indicators.note: something under construction is still being assembled, so these letters are being put together in a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A monstrous highway being built in America.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinosaur is a huge prehistoric reptile, the archetypal monster of the ancient world.

clue.text: Very bad, extremely low-grade record

indicators.note: extremely here means at the extremes, so only the two end letters of the following word are kept

blocks.note: colloquially chronic means dreadful, very bad
the outer letters of low-grade

explanation.surface: A dreadful, utterly substandard performance being recorded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' looks like an intensifier for low-grade, but it picks out its ends.
explanation.definitionFit: A chronicle is a written account of events in order, a historical record.

clue.text: Biting lip in the forefront

blocks.note: a cutting remark is a biting one
the lip of something is its edge or rim

explanation.surface: A sharp-tongued mouth leading the way.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting-edge describes the most advanced work in a field, leading at the forefront of development.

clue.text: A guru primarily brought in to criticise a heathen

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of the word before it is used
being brought in to something means going inside it, so these letters sit within the next word

blocks.note: taken as written
first letter of guru
to pan a show is to criticise it harshly

explanation.surface: A spiritual teacher is called in to condemn an unbeliever.
explanation.definitionFit: A pagan is someone outside the main world religions, an older word for a heathen.

clue.text: Occasionally misplaced coronet with diamonds on it

indicators.note: things misplaced are put in the wrong position, so these letters are moved out of their order

blocks.note: taken as written
W is a standard abbreviation for with
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: Every so often someone mislays a diamond-studded small crown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' contributes a letter of its own rather than joining things up: W is short for with.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something once or twice means doing it only a few times, now and then, i.e. occasionally.

clue.text: Terribly bad — summon one who looks into complaints

indicators.note: terribly means in an awful way, so the letters are put in an awful mess

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dreadful call-up, investigated by an official who hears grievances.
explanation.definitionFit: An ombudsman is an official appointed to investigate grievances against organisations or public bodies.

clue.text: Old Cornish drink from the wood

blocks.note: first meaning: a historic Cornish mix of gin and treacle
second meaning: a reddish-brown tropical hardwood

explanation.surface: An old West Country tipple served out of the barrel.
explanation.walkthrough: The drink is obscure: Cornish fishermen's gin sweetened with treacle, named for its colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahogany is a valuable dark timber used for furniture, and also the name of that old Cornish drink.

clue.text: Punk in fleece, boss man

blocks.note: to fleece someone is to skin them, cheat them of money
the head is the person in charge

explanation.surface: A young rebel in a fleece jacket working as the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: A skinhead is a youth of a shaven-headed subculture, an aggressive young hooligan, so a punk in the slang sense.

clue.text: Famous radical novelist from Scotland, one who has many good ideas

definitions.text: one who has many good ideas

blocks.note: John Bright was a celebrated Victorian Radical politician and orator
Muriel Spark was a Scottish novelist, author of The Prime of Miss Jean Brodie

explanation.surface: A list of distinguished Britons, one of them full of inspiration.
explanation.walkthrough: John Bright, a nineteenth-century campaigner against the Corn Laws, and Muriel Spark, the Edinburgh-born novelist, are joined end to end.
explanation.definitionFit: A bright spark is an informal term for a clever, lively person full of ideas, sometimes said ironically.

clue.text: Chap shattered leg in rolling-press

indicators.note: something shattered is broken into pieces, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: a chap is a man
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man broke his leg in a laundry wringer.
explanation.definitionFit: A mangle is a machine with rollers for pressing water out of washing, a press that works by rolling.

clue.text: Record about girl being drunk

indicators.note: about means around, so the record's letters go round the name

blocks.note: a CD is a compact disc, a recording
a girl's name

explanation.surface: An album recorded about a girl who's intoxicated.
explanation.definitionFit: Canned is British slang for drunk, like tinned or bottled.

clue.text: A flipping draw helps one get trophy

indicators.note: flipping something over turns it the other way, so the following word is read from back to front

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A frustrating tied match still earns a team a cup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' poses as a mild British curse word on draw; it is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An award is a prize such as a cup or medal, so a trophy is one kind of award.

clue.text: Inexperienced youth with new musical instrument

blocks.note: green means new or unripe
a horn is a brass instrument

explanation.surface: A beginner turning up with a freshly bought instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A greenhorn is a naive newcomer lacking experience, typically a young novice.

clue.text: Arrest old boy, a very wealthy person

blocks.note: to nab is to catch or arrest
OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: Police detain a former pupil who is extremely rich.
explanation.definitionFit: A nabob was originally a Mughal governor; it came to mean a man who made a fortune in India, hence any rich person.

clue.text: Nervous men, edgy about a Trojan youth

indicators.note: nervous suggests jittery and unsettled, so the letters are jumbled into a new order
about means around, so the jumbled letters go round the single letter that follows

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Anxious, tense men gathered round a young man of Troy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Edgy' sits beside nervous as if both describe the men, but it is fodder; only 'Nervous' signals the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Ganymede was a beautiful Trojan prince carried off by Zeus to be cupbearer to the gods.

clue.text: Bishop trapped in a lounge on fire

indicators.note: something trapped in another thing is held inside it, so the letter sits within the following words

blocks.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
taken as written
to lounge about is to laze

explanation.surface: A clergyman caught in a burning sitting room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lounge' reads as a room but works as a verb meaning to idle.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ablaze is burning fiercely, which is what on fire means.

clue.text: Threaten to put a stop to nark

blocks.note: to end something is to put a stop to it
to nark is British slang for annoy

explanation.surface: Warning that you will shut down a police informer.
explanation.walkthrough: A nark is also British slang for a police informer, which is the picture; here it is the verb meaning to irritate.
explanation.definitionFit: To endanger something is to put it at risk, which is to threaten its safety.

clue.text: Complied with demands, making love with you in bed

indicators.note: in places the word before it inside the word after it

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O
ye is the old form of you
taken as written

explanation.surface: Doing what was asked, making love with you in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who obeyed carried out what was ordered, i.e. complied with the demands made.
